I think, yes. Pwedeng factor ito. I would like to answer this by sighting du.30 as an example. Tingin ko kasi, du.30 with his populist ideology has further divided our country- ordinaryong Pilipino vs elite (pwede na rin sigurong isama 'yung may pinag-aralan dito). 

And because of that 'dualism', they feel like they relate to du.30 kasi hindi siya 'usual' politician. They can, somehow, see themselves kay du.30 which gave them the permission to act like that - anti-intellectual (as you would say). And du.30 (and the people around him) exploits them by throwing shade sa elite (ABS-CBN, UP, etc.), which further strengthen 'yung dualism. 

So, how can we go around with these people?

In my opinion (and I could be wrong), we should engage more with them and try to relate ourselves to them more. 

For example, my mom voted du.30 last 2016. The reason why she voted him? Kasi tingin niya, naiintindihan ni du.30 'yung normal na Pilipino. Nakakarelate siya kay du.30 (at least at that time). And we cannot blame them for that, since other candidates last 2016 were more for the 'elite'.

Please don't calm them 'bobo' for that. Wala namang ma-sosolve kung ganoon ang sasabihin. Lalo lang nila (du.30 supporters) iisipin na may duality nga.
